messages:
perf-bot: CI microbench failed on pr/12981 — kv_warmup_hitrate dropped 18% vs main (threshold 5%). full CI: https://ci.internal/arch/12981

alex: saw the alert, looks like kernel-selector touched in the PR?

maya: ugh, that PR changed the kernel priority table. did we add any new heuristics?

sanjay: quick profile I ran on the failing CI image — warmup gets fewer KV hits early. flamegraph shows extra memcpy path in kernel A vs kernel B. command I used:
```
./bench --suite=kv_warmup --runs=200 --histogram
# capture with perf and infer-flame
perf record -F 99 -g ./bench && infer-flame perf.data > fg.svg
```

lee: can we reproduce locally? CI numbers are noisy but 18% seems real.

alex: maya, can you run the same bench on your machine with the new PR?

maya: running now, but my machine is macbook so noisy — will spin up a linux x86 in cloud.

perf-bot: attach: /artifacts/pr-12981/kv_warmup/bench.log (stderr included)

alex: log shows selector choosing kernelA for ~60% of short sequences where previously kernelB was 90%. kernelA has suboptimal kv cache prefetch path.

sanjay: hypothesis: change in kernel scoring moved some short-seq traffic to kernelA which doesn't use prefix KV prefetch. I can try forcing kernelB to verify.

lee: +1 to force test. If that repros, either revert the scoring tweak or add a short-seq rule for kv-prefetch.

maya: repro on linux VM: baseline (main) kv_hit 92%, pr build kv_hit 74%. Forcing kernelB on the same inputs brings it back to 91%.

alex: good repro. next step: git bisect between main@a1f2 and pr merge commit to find offending commit. leaving to sanjay unless someone volunteers.

sanjay: I'll take the bisect. plan: binary search with the microbench. If we find the commit, we can either revert or patch scoring to prefer prefetchable kernels for short sequences.

lee: also add a unit perf test that asserts kv_warmup_hitrate doesn't drop by >5% for standard prompt set — fail early on merges.

perf-bot: CI comment posted on PR: "microbench kv_warmup hitrate regression detected — investigating (assigned: sanjay)" :mag: 

alex: thanks. sanjay—post updates here when you have the culprit commit or if you need infra for faster bisect (more VMs).

sanjay: will update in ~2 hours after first pass. if it's the selector heuristic I can propose a small score delta + coverage tests.

maya: added a quick smoke script to reproduce locally: `scripts/repro_kv_warmup.sh` (uses docker image from CI). share after sanjay picks this up. :thumbsup:

lee: if revert needed and it's low-risk, we'll cut an emergency revert and run canary for 4 hours.

alex: sounds good. folks keep thread updated.
